svg.aria-label: Two pointers mechanism map: opposite-ends convergence, and eleven variant diagrams.
svg.text: Sliding window is two pointers moving the SAME direction with a gap. This module is everything
else: pointers converging from opposite ends, walking two sequences, or partitioning in place.
R / right / high / lead pointer (or 2nd sequence)

g.text: L moves right — rule decides when
R moves left — rule decides when

svg.text: L and R start at opposite ends and move inward. What differs between variants is the RULE that
decides which one moves next: a comparison, a greedy bound, or a partition invariant.
What differs is the rule, the direction, or how many sequences

g.text: Sum too big → R steps in; too
small → L steps out. Sorted order
rules out a whole row per step.
Area is capped by the shorter
wall. Moving the taller one can't
once its own cell is classified.
Each pointer walks its own array.
No target to search for — only
every step is the same swap.
gap = n, constant from the start
Gap is fixed before the walk
hits the end, trail is n behind.
value is. Each swap moves one
element to its side, in O(n).
